questions.enonce_markdown: Complete the table by calculating the values for total revenue. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Total revenue (TR) is price multiplied by the quantity bought: $TR = P \times Q_d$. Because the quantity is in thousands of sachets, TR is in thousands of FCFA ('000 FCFA).

| Price (FCFA) | Quantity demanded (000) | Quantity supplied (000) | Total revenue ('000 FCFA) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 80 | 0 | 100 | $80 \times 0 = 0$ |
| 70 | 20 | 100 | $70 \times 20 = 1\,400$ |
| 60 | 40 | 100 | $60 \times 40 = 2\,400$ |
| 50 | 60 | 100 | $50 \times 60 = 3\,000$ |
| 40 | 80 | 100 | $40 \times 80 = 3\,200$ |
| 30 | 100 | 100 | $30 \times 100 = 3\,000$ |
| 20 | 120 | 100 | $20 \times 120 = 2\,400$ |
| 10 | 140 | 100 | $10 \times 140 = 1\,400$ |

Total revenue rises as the price falls from 80 to 40 (demand is elastic there), is highest at a price of 40 FCFA (3 200 thousand FCFA, that is 3.2 million FCFA), then falls as the price falls further (demand is inelastic).

questions.enonce_markdown:
i) With the use of a graph paper plot the demand and supply curves for sachet tomatoes. (6 marks)

ii) What is the equilibrium market price and why? (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)**

**Plotting the curves.** Put **price (FCFA)** on the vertical axis (0 to 80, 10 FCFA per square) and **quantity (thousands of sachets)** on the horizontal axis (0 to 140 or 160, 20 per square). Give the graph a title and label both axes and both curves.

- **Demand curve (D):** plot the points (0, 80), (20, 70), (40, 60), (60, 50), (80, 40), (100, 30), (120, 20), (140, 10) and join them. It is a **straight line sloping downwards** (the demand schedule is $Q_d = 160 - 2P$): as the price falls, the quantity demanded rises.
- **Supply curve (S):** the quantity supplied is 100 at every price, so S is a **vertical straight line at Q = 100** (perfectly inelastic supply).

The two curves cross at the point **E (Q = 100, P = 30)**.

![fig-1](gce-al-economics-2026-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2_fig_1.png)

*(Marking: 2 marks for correct axes and scales, 2 for the demand curve, 2 for the supply curve.)*

**(ii)**

The **equilibrium market price is 30 FCFA** per sachet (equilibrium quantity 100 000 sachets).

**Why:** the equilibrium price is the price at which the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied. At 30 FCFA, $Q_d = Q_s = 100$ (thousand), so there is neither a surplus nor a shortage and no pressure for the price to change. At any price above 30 FCFA, supply (100) exceeds demand, so unsold sachets force sellers to cut the price. At any price below 30 FCFA, demand exceeds supply (a shortage), so buyers bid the price up. Both forces push the price back to 30 FCFA.

Check with the demand function: $160 - 2P = 100 \Rightarrow P = 30$.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the time period in which the suppliers of sachet tomatoes are operating? Give your reason. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The suppliers are operating in the **market period (the very short run)**.

**Reason:** the quantity supplied is **fixed at 100 000 sachets at every price**, so supply is perfectly inelastic (a vertical supply curve). In the market period the tomatoes have already been harvested and packed; producers cannot increase output in response to a higher price because no factor of production can be varied and tomatoes are perishable, so they cannot be held back for long either. Only in the short run (some factors variable) or the long run (all factors variable) can supply respond to price.

questions.enonce_markdown: If the government sets a maximum price of 10 FCFA per sachet of tomatoes list four advantages of such a price legislation to the public. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A maximum price (price ceiling) of 10 FCFA is far below the equilibrium price of 30 FCFA, so it is effective. Four advantages to the public (consumers), 1 mark each:

1. **Lower price and greater affordability:** a sachet costs 10 FCFA instead of 30 FCFA, so low-income households can buy tomatoes.
2. **Higher real income and living standards:** the money saved can be spent on other goods, which raises the consumers' real purchasing power.
3. **Higher consumption and better nutrition:** the quantity demanded rises from 100 000 to 140 000 sachets, so more households can afford this food.
4. **Protection against exploitation:** consumers are shielded from profiteering by sellers when supply is short (for example, off-season), and the cost of living and inflationary pressure are contained.

(Also accepted: reduced income inequality, higher consumer surplus for those who manage to buy, stable prices.)

*Remark:* at 10 FCFA the quantity supplied (100 000) is less than the quantity demanded (140 000), so there is a shortage of 40 000 sachets: this may lead to queues, rationing and a black market, which are the disadvantages of the measure (not asked here).
